Chapter 108: The Campus Network is About to Start its Closed Beta

After coming back from Professor Yuan's, Chen Guiliang couldn't make it to his next class.

There was still enough time, but there would definitely be no seats left. He could only stand in the hallway outside and listen.

Might as well skip class.

Chen Guiliang rode his bike straight back to the dorm. As he went upstairs, he heard someone yell "Attack," "Dodge," and he immediately grabbed his digital camera and ran over.

The digital camera was purchased last weekend.

Quite expensive.

Entry-level ones cost 1,500–3,000 yuan, and the image quality was tragic.

Mid-range models were 3,000–6,000 yuan, with decent performance.

Anything over 6,000 yuan wasn't worth mentioning.

Chen Guiliang bought a Japanese brand camera for 3,500 yuan, with 5 megapixels, 3x zoom, and video recording support.

Specifically for promotional use.

He followed the voices to the end of the dormitory hallway and found five male students sitting there, snacking on sunflower seeds and playing Legends of the Three Kingdoms.

The old dorms were very shabby; the hallway was a major public social area.

Especially in a building like Dorm 36, where there wasn't even enough space to store daily necessities. Many students simply placed their thermoses and washbasin stands out in the hallway.

The Yuanpei Program was better, with four people to a room.

Students from other departments even had six- or eight-person rooms.

"Can I take a few pictures?" Chen Guiliang asked.

A rebel who had already been killed off asked, "Pictures of what?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Of you guys playing Legends of the Three Kingdoms, to upload to the BBS. I'm the creator of the game, and I want to promote it a little. If you're not willing, that's fine. I can also avoid showing your faces."

"You made Legends of the Three Kingdoms? Dude, you're awesome!"

"Quick, come sit down and chat."

"Go ahead and shoot, what's there for a bunch of guys to be afraid of?"

"Remember to make me look handsome."

The lighting in the hallway was dim, so Chen Guiliang used the flash, snapping several photos with a series of clicks.

After some casual conversation, Chen Guiliang returned to his own dorm room.

He turned on his computer and logged into both the Peking University and Tsinghua University BBS forums. He was using a new account now, with the screen name "Classmate Xiao Tao."

"Maple Sympathy" was for trolling.

"Classmate Xiao Tao" was for promotion.

Chen Guiliang uploaded the photos and created a post with the title: "SHOCKING: Peking University students actually doing this kind of thing in their dorm building!!!"

He had already made dozens of promotional posts about Legends of the Three Kingdoms over the past few days.

There were also detailed explanations of the rules, with photos of every card uploaded and addresses of stores where the cards could be purchased.

Chen Guiliang tabbed out and continued writing *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*. After half an hour, he checked the replies.

"What the heck is with this title? I clicked in all excited just to see a few guys playing cards?"

"SHOCKING: Classmate Xiao Tao has posted again!"

"The OP is even more obnoxious than Sister Furong. I really want to beat him up."

"Let's discuss, is Classmate Xiao Tao a guy or a girl?"

"Reply to the post above: A ladyboy."

"I've played Legends of the Three Kingdoms in the club activity room. It's pretty fun, I was just planning to buy a set."

"30 yuan a set is still too expensive."

"So bored. Anyone want to play Legends of the Three Kingdoms? Location: graduate student dorm."

Just as Chen Guiliang was about to switch accounts to reply, his phone suddenly rang.

It was a call from the Peking University Press Reader Service Department. This store mainly sold Peking University textbooks, academic monographs, and books on humanities and social sciences. At the time, its address was still near the Triangle, a prime location.

Chen Guiliang had talked himself hoarse before they finally agreed to help sell the game on consignment, and even then, they only kept five sets in the store.

Because Legends of the Three Kingdoms came in a box, it took up quite a bit of space.

"Hello, Boss Chen. This is the Reader Service Department." His form of address had even changed; before, they had always called him "Classmate Chen Guiliang."

"Hello."

"Those 5 sets of Legends of the Three Kingdoms sold out yesterday. This morning, two more students came asking about it. I'd like to order another 50 sets, and if sales are good, we'll order more."

"Okay, I'll have them delivered right away."

Chen Guiliang's mood instantly brightened. This was the first consignment store to request a restock.

The situation was gradually opening up.

Chen Guiliang quickly called Guo Feng.

He had already found a delivery person. There were people in the Peking University Science Park who specialized in this kind of work. But they were employees of the Science Park company, so delivering for Chen Guiliang was a side job, and paying per trip was not cost-effective.

Once sales of Legends of the Three Kingdoms improved and various retail stores were willing to stock more, the delivery costs could be minimized. They could just restock at a fixed time, delivering to several stores in one trip—by a three-wheeled flatbed tricycle.

Only Guo Feng had the authority to take the games from the warehouse in the Science Park. When he needed to get them, he just had to call the warehouse manager.

Sigh, he still needed to hire someone to handle miscellaneous tasks. He couldn't always trouble Guo Feng with this stuff.

The wages for part-time jobs for Peking University students were too high; he needed to hire a full-time employee from off-campus.

Chen Guiliang called the incubator company's service department again, entrusting them to find someone reliable. In the future, restock calls would be directed to the office landline; otherwise, Chen Guiliang would be annoyed to death.

Just then, another call came in requesting a restock.

Chen Guiliang had no choice but to call Guo Feng again.

"Aren't you annoying?" Guo Feng was already getting a little fed up.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm hiring someone. You won't have to be bothered for much longer."

Guo Feng said, "Even when you've hired someone, don't have them call my landline here. Hurry up and rent another office."

Chen Guiliang said, "The new building in the Science Park is already undergoing basic renovations. I'll rent a bigger space then, and we can move in after some redecorating. We can all go breathe in the fresh formaldehyde together."

The rent for the new office building was even cheaper than this shabby office because it had just been built. Leaving it empty was a waste, so they might as well lease it to incubator companies on the cheap.

The preferential rate Project Manager Wang Kai applied for was 20 yuan per square meter per month. As the number of resident companies increased, the price would surely go up.

Note, this was billed monthly, not daily.

Twenty years later, it would be 6–10 yuan per square meter per day. Even so, the price was lower than surrounding office buildings.

After chatting for a bit, Guo Feng said, "The campus network can start its closed beta test tomorrow. The main goal is to test cross-browser compatibility, resolve database read/write bottlenecks, and optimize page load speeds. We'll also do some security checks and validate the core modules of the website..."

Chen Guiliang only half-understood what he was hearing, but he didn't interrupt, patiently listening until he finished. "How many people do you need to participate?"

"The initial test will require about 100 to 500 people," Guo Feng said. "I can probably invite twenty or thirty. You'll need to take care of the rest. If there really aren't enough people, we can give the first batch of invitees some invitation codes and have them each invite one or two friends."

"I'll invite as many as I can." The time to test Chen Guiliang's network of contacts had come.

Guo Feng said, "I'll send you the URL and invitation codes tonight. Remember to have them send feedback via email. Tell them to report any problems they encounter right away."

Chen Guiliang had a huge number of contacts saved in his phone.

His QQ and email contact lists were also exploding with people. This guy had been making preparations ever since he started university, and now it was finally paying off.

That night, Chen Guiliang skipped class again.

He replied to emails one by one, many of which were from people who had discussed classical poetry with him.

Chen Guiliang replied to each one earnestly. No matter how poorly written, he would find an angle to praise it. Then he would tactfully suggest revisions, adding that he didn't know much himself and hoped they could all improve together in the future.

If he came across a well-written one, he would shamelessly lavish it with praise, trying to flatter the person to the heavens. What was there to correct? No revisions needed; not a single word should be changed for a thousand pieces of gold!

At the end of each email, he attached an invitation code and a URL.

He adopted a humble tone, saying he had started a website that needed testing but couldn't find anyone trustworthy. Although they had only met once or twice, Chen Guiliang felt an instant connection with them and knew they were people who could be entrusted with important matters.

Blah, blah, blah.

Next, he went through his QQ and phone contacts, leaving messages one by one...

After this whole operation, Chen Guiliang was exhausted. He lay on his bed and called Bian Guanyue. "Are you out of class?"

"Just got back to the dorm," Bian Guanyue said.

Chen Guiliang asked, "How have things been lately?"

Bian Guanyue said, "I ran into a really annoying senior. He's like glue; I can't shake him off. I've already told him I have a boyfriend, but he's still so shameless. I'm about to lose my mind over this guy!"

"I'll come over this weekend. You should ask him out to dinner," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue reminded him, "Don't you dare hit him. If things blow up, it'll be hard to handle. Peking University might even find out."

Chen Guiliang laughed. "Am I that unreasonable of a person? I'm just going to sell him a set of Legends of the Three Kingdoms."

Selling Legends of the Three Kingdoms to a love rival?

Bian Guanyue didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

Chen Guiliang continued, "That senior probably isn't a bad person. He's just too bored, that's why he's clinging to you. My Legends of the Three Kingdoms is very fun. It can occupy his excess energy and enrich his university life."

"You're such a smooth talker," Bian Guanyue couldn't help but laugh.

Chen Guiliang said, "The campus network starts its beta test tomorrow. I'll send you an invitation code. Go check it out when you have time. I'll be registering with my real name too, so we can add each other as friends."

"Okay, we can chat on the campus network," Bian Guanyue said with anticipation, mainly because the website belonged to her boyfriend.

After chatting for a while, Chen Guiliang hung up only when Senior Min and Jiang Junlai returned to the dorm.

"Boss Chen, can I use your computer?" Min Wenyu said.

The nickname "Boss Chen" was now spreading far and wide.

Lying on his bed, Chen Guiliang said, "Go ahead."

Min Wenyu pressed the spacebar to wake the screen, and the email client appeared before him. "Whoa, how many emails have you received? Do you have to know this many people to do business?"

"The campus network is testing tomorrow. I'm inviting them to participate in the closed beta," Chen Guiliang explained.

Jiang Junlai was surprised. "It's done already? I want to join the closed beta too!"

"Anyone who wants to join will get an invitation code," Chen Guiliang said. "Go ahead and close my email."

Senior Min had bought a computer in his freshman year, a secondhand one for a few hundred yuan, but sold it because it was affecting his studies.

Now he used Chen Guiliang's computer every day.

Chen Guiliang thought for a moment, then sent a text message to the incubator project manager, Wang Kai: "Teacher Wang, the campus network will be in closed beta tomorrow. You are welcome to come and provide your guidance."

Wang Kai replied instantly: "You guys are fast. I'll definitely come and observe."

Chen Guiliang sent a few more compliments, then tossed his phone aside and lay on his bed, not wanting to move.

Dealing with all this tonight was more mentally exhausting than a full day of classes.

He actually preferred to be a carefree spirit, writing something to earn money whenever he was broke.

But having been reborn, he felt unwilling to not start a business.

(End of this chapter)
